section_summary: This section covers Japan’s postwar political parties, occupation policy, economic recovery, and concerns about a return to militarism. It also contains correspondence about neighborhood associations and a substantial set of translated rules for the Japanese Diet. Several telegrams and airgrams are represented only by fragmentary or poorly legible OCR.

subfiles.title: Preliminary Study of the Neighborhood Associations of Japan
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a study of the wartime tonarigumi and their postwar abolition.
subfiles.summary: Reports that abolition was virtually complete by June 1947; the enclosed study is not present in this section.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Editorial from Times on Japanese Political Parties
subfiles.about: Forwards a Times editorial about Katayama’s resignation.
subfiles.summary: Attributes Katayama’s fall partly to loss of support from his party’s Socialist wing.

subfiles.title: Parties in Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses Katayama’s coalition and possible successor governments.
subfiles.summary: Describes the coalition’s internal divisions, Katayama’s reforms, and the possibility of a Yoshida-led conservative coalition.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Shanghai concerning Japanese rearmament
subfiles.about: Conveys objections to military installations and training in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR questions whether naval bases, airfields, pilot training, and industrial restoration accord with Japan’s peaceful postwar obligations. Much of the telegram is illegible.

subfiles.title: Incoming telegram 5728
subfiles.about: Records receipt of an incoming telegram.
subfiles.summary: Routing information survives, but the telegram’s substance is not legible.

subfiles.title: Response to Questions Submitted to General MacArthur by a Representative of Central News Agency of China
subfiles.about: Forwards Shen’s questions and Sebald’s MacArthur-approved answers.
subfiles.summary: Sebald encloses the February 24 inquiry and his February 27 reply.

subfiles.title: Questions to General MacArthur
subfiles.about: Requests answers for Chinese readers about Japan after occupation.
subfiles.summary: Asks about renewed militarism, occupation problems, democracy, political leadership, and communism.

subfiles.title: Reply to James C. Y. Shen
subfiles.about: Answers Shen’s four questions on Japan’s postwar future.
subfiles.summary: Sebald argues that disarmament makes renewed militarism remote, economic self-sufficiency requires trade and Allied cooperation, democracy will endure, and improved conditions will limit communism.

subfiles.title: Incoming telegram received February 28
subfiles.about: Records receipt of a telegram concerning Japan.
subfiles.summary: Only fragmentary routing and message text are legible.

subfiles.title: London airgram on the Japanese political situation
subfiles.about: Discusses Ashida’s selection and alignments among Japanese parties.
subfiles.summary: Describes Liberal opposition to a Socialist coalition, Ashida’s middle course, press criticism, and concern over Communist influence in unions. The first page is largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Situation and Problems in Japan
subfiles.about: Records Sherwood Fine’s assessment of Japan’s politics and economy.
subfiles.summary: Fine connects cabinet instability and ideological conflict to inflation and wider economic distress. He discusses reparations, trade barriers, food and textile supply, United States aid, and SCAP recovery planning. He argues that recovery requires a clear long-term program and expanding Japanese responsibility for its administration.

subfiles.title: Corrected incoming telegram
subfiles.about: Marks an incoming telegram as a corrected copy.
subfiles.summary: The message itself is not legible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Voided incoming telegram copy
subfiles.about: Identifies a telegram copy as void in favor of an attached corrected copy.
subfiles.summary: The sheet directs readers to the corrected copy.

subfiles.title: London airgram on Japanese party politics
subfiles.about: Apparently discusses the Liberal Party and formation of a government.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text is too damaged to establish its argument securely.

subfiles.title: Rules and Election Laws, Japanese Diet
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards four Government Section publications on Diet rules and election laws.
subfiles.summary: Lists rules for both Diet houses and election laws for their members.

subfiles.title: Rules of the House of Representatives
subfiles.from: Government Section, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets out the rules adopted for Japan’s House of Representatives.
subfiles.summary: The rules cover selection of officers and a prime minister, bills, committees, public hearings, plenary debate, voting, petitions, attendance, qualifications, records, visitors, discipline, and relations with the House of Councillors and government offices. Helen Loeb edited this copy on March 2, 1948.

subfiles.title: Rules of the House of Councillors
subfiles.from: Government Section, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Begins the rules adopted for Japan’s House of Councillors.
subfiles.summary: Only the title page and part of the contents appear here; the document continues beyond page 366.
